'''Howard Mark Wiseman''' (born 19 June 1968) is an Australian [[theoretical physics|theoretical]] and [[quantum physicist]], who is notable for his work on [[Coherent control|quantum feedback control]], [[quantum measurement]]s, [[quantum information]] (especially [[quantum steering]]), [[open quantum system]]s, the [[Many-worlds interpretation|many interacting worlds interpretation]] of quantum mechanics,<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevX.4.041013|title = Quantum Phenomena Modeled by Interactions between Many Classical Worlds|journal = Physical Review X|volume = 4|issue = 4|article-number = 041013|year = 2014|last1 = Hall|first1 = Michael J. W.|last2 = Deckert|first2 = Dirk-André|last3 = Wiseman|first3 = Howard M.|bibcode = 2014PhRvX...4d1013H|arxiv = 1402.6144|s2cid = 55130578}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | url=http://www.nature.com/news/a-quantum-world-arising-from-many-ordinary-ones-1.16213 |doi = 10.1038/nature.2014.16213|title = A quantum world arising from many ordinary ones|journal = Nature|year = 2014|last1 = Witze|first1 = Alexandra|s2cid = 124694221|url-access = subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://theconversation.com/when-parallel-worlds-collide-quantum-mechanics-is-born-32631 |title = When parallel worlds collide ... Quantum mechanics is born| date=24 October 2014 }}</ref> and other topics in [[quantum foundations]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.cqc2t.org/biography/104 |title = Wiseman, Author at CQC2T}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Wiseman was born in [[Brisbane]], [[Australia]] and received his B.Sc.(Hons) in Physics from the [[University of Queensland]] in 1991. He completed his PhD in physics under [[Gerard J. Milburn]] at the [[University of Queensland]] in 1994, with a thesis entitled ''Quantum Trajectories and Feedback.''<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120630213751/http://library.uq.edu.au/search~S7?/awiseman,+h/awiseman+h/1,9,24,B/frameset&FF=awiseman+howard+mark&1,1,|title=Wiseman's thesis}}</ref>

== Career ==
After his PhD, Wiseman  undertook a postdoc under [[Daniel Frank Walls|Dan Walls]] at the [[University of Auckland]]. From 1996 to 2009 he held [[Australian Research Council]] (ARC) research fellowships. He is currently a Physics Professor at [[Griffith University]], where he is the Director of the ''Centre for Quantum Dynamics''. He is also an Executive Node Manager in the ''Centre for Quantum Computation and Communication Technology'', an ARC Centre of Excellence.

== Honors ==
His early-career awards include the [[William Lawrence Bragg|Bragg Medal]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.aip.org.au/bragg-medal | title=The Australian Institute of Physics - BRAGG MEDAL }}</ref> of the [[Australian Institute of Physics]] (AIP), the [[Pawsey Medal]] of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] and the Malcolm Macintosh Medal, one of the [[Prime Minister's Prizes for Science]]. He is a [[list of Fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]], a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], and a Fellow of [[The Optical Society|The Optical Society of America]]. In 2022 Wiseman was awarded the AIP's [[Walter Boas Medal|Walter Boas Medal for Excellence in Research]], ''for elucidating fundamental limits arising from quantum theory, in particular in its applications to metrology and laser science, and via its implications for the foundations of reality.''<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.aip.org.au/News/12433388 | title=The Australian Institute of Physics - Congratulations to our 2021 AIP Medal winners }}</ref>
